Oracle ruling under review (attack it too): IEEE 1800-2017 §26.3 ("locally visible … declared prior to that point within the current scope"; Example 1: a generate block reading `x` before its own `int x` binds the outer `p::x`), §6.5 ("declared before they are used"). iverilog follows it (lexical; refuses a forward parameter or binds the outer one); sv2v and verilator are scope-wide and disagree with the LRM example Z0a — treated as disqualified on forward references. Under the IEEE model: 45 up, 0 down on 149 cells; under the sv2v+verilator model 7 OK→LOUD (F3 I4 M4 V04 V24s Z1f Z5m) — claimed correct-loud by IEEE.

HIT OUTSIDE THE TABLE.

Every lens answers: does the product shake (a new silent-wrong; a correct→loud on a design IEEE makes legal; a determinism or staged/one-shot divergence; a crash)? A loud on a design whose forward reference IEEE §26.3 makes illegal is correct-loud only when the IEEE text clearly covers the shape (parameters, localparams, genvars, nets, typedefs, functions — function/task calls are EXEMPT from declare-before-use in §26.3: "For a reference to an identifier other than function or task call" — check that the mismatch path never fires on a forward FUNCTION call or hierarchical reference that IEEE resolves after elaboration (§23.8 upward/hierarchical names)). For each finding: new vs known class; PRE | POST | iverilog | verilator | sv2v raw; IEEE clause; 4-way; attribution re-measured on PRE.
Severity: BLOCKING / MAJOR (false claim in docs/comments/diagnostic text/commit) / MINOR (residue).
Budget: ≤60 tool calls, ≤40 designed cells. Return findings in your final message (REPORT.md writes may be refused; try $S/s592/r1/<lens>/REPORT.md first).
